title: Notion vs Obsidian for a two-person company wiki

entries.query_str: notion vs obsidian for a shared wiki between 2 cofounders. we need meeting notes, a reading list, and product specs. no budget
entries.answer:
For two people who need to **share and co-edit**, Notion is usually the easier default; Obsidian shines for a single person's linked notes [1][2].

| | Notion (free plan) | Obsidian |
|---|---|---|
| Real-time co-editing | Yes, built in | No; needs Obsidian Sync (paid) or a git/Dropbox workaround [2] |
| Databases (reading list with status, tags) | Native databases with views | Via community plugins (Dataview), more setup |
| Offline / local files | Limited; cloud-first | Plain Markdown files on disk, fully offline [1] |
| Free plan limits | Free for individuals; small teams can use the free tier with block/guest limits [3] | Free for personal use |
| Lock-in | Export to Markdown/CSV, some formatting loss | None — it's just files |

**Suggestion:** a Notion teamspace with three databases — *Meetings* (date, attendees, decisions), *Reading list* (status, who's reading, link), *Specs* (owner, status). If one of you prefers Obsidian for private thinking, keep that personal and paste conclusions into Notion.

entries.query_str: can notion databases link to each other like a spec linking to the meeting where we decided it
entries.answer: Yes — use a **Relation** property [1]. Add a "Decided in" relation on the *Specs* database pointing to *Meetings*; Notion creates the reverse relation automatically, so each meeting page shows which specs it produced. Add a **Rollup** if you want, e.g., the date of the most recent related meeting on each spec [1][2]. One caveat: relations only work between databases in the same workspace, so keep both in the shared teamspace.
